messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple decode nodes reporting CUDA OOMs and streaming request drops. Alerting SRE oncall. error_sample=cudaErrorOutOfMemory

Maya Cheng: acked. I'm on it. Paging SRE channel, starting triage.

Samir Patel: seeing the same in logs, a bunch of `decode-worker` pods hitting OOM during streaming. stack snippet: ```ERROR decode: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-15T14:12:10Z decode-worker-42: pid=1123 tid=47 cudaErrorOutOfMemory at n_ctx=5120 requested=8192MB```

Leo Nguyen: any recent deploy? config change?

Maya Cheng: no code deploy in last hour. We rotated capacity earlier but that was autoscale. Notice a spike in long-running streams — looks like some requests never capped `max_tokens`.

Tara Jenkins: Customer reports: AcmePay saw 500s and dropped responses ~14:12-14:18. They opened a support ticket.

Samir Patel: digging. Querying request logs for `max_tokens` header. Running: ```select count(*) from requests where max_tokens > 4096 and ts > '2026-03-15T14:00:00Z'```

ops-bot: query complete — 174 requests with max_tokens >= 65536 between 14:05 and 14:15 UTC. Top callers: frontend-service-legacy (internal), thirdparty-integration (external).

Maya Cheng: that explains it — runaway generation. Some client is overriding max_tokens to huge values; decode stays in streaming until OOM. Need quick mitigations: rate-limit long streams, enforce soft max at proxy, and drain affected nodes.

Leo Nguyen: proposed immediate actions: 1) update gateway to reject max_tokens > 8192 with 400 + logging 2) put autoscaler on conservative mode 3) cordon problematic nodes and restart pods 4) fallback traffic to smaller model variant.

Samir Patel: I'm pushing a temporary nginx/gateway patch to clamp tokens. Patch: ```diff --git a/gateway b/gateway
@@
- accepted_max = req.headers.get('x-max-tokens', 0)
+ accepted_max = min(int(req.headers.get('x-max-tokens', 0) or 0), 8192)
``` Deploying to canary now.

Maya Cheng: @Samir can you also enable `stream_timeout=120s` to avoid forever streams?

Samir Patel: done. Canary shows immediate drop in long-duration streams. Logs: ```INFO gateway: clamped max_tokens from 65536 to 8192 for req id=abc123```

ops-bot: canary health ok, rolling to prod in 30s.

Tara Jenkins: coordinating with AcmePay support. They confirm fewer 500s after 14:20. Still seeing intermittent 503s while pods recycle.

Leo Nguyen: cordoning nodes with repeated OOMs. Commands used: ```kubectl cordon node/gpu-decode-7a && kubectl drain node/gpu-decode-7a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``` Restarting decode pods onto healthy hosts.

Samir Patel: also enabling model fallback for heavy requests: redirect to redwood-mini-quant for requests > 4096 tokens. Patch applied to routing table.

Maya Cheng: after these: OOM count dropped 95% in 5 minutes, request error rate back to baseline. Current mitigation status: gateway clamp + stream timeout + cordon/restart + model fallback.

ops-bot: monitoring metrics: decode_oom_count 14:10->14:30: 230 -> 12. request_5xx_rate dropped from 3.6% -> 0.4%.

Tara Jenkins: customer impact summary for AcmePay: partial — they experienced failed transactions for ~6 minutes, then degraded but functional. Support has opened an incident ticket and offered a post-incident call.

Leo Nguyen: root cause candidate: upstream client had a bug that sent `x-max-tokens: 100000` due to defaulting logic in their SDK; our gateway allowed it through. We'll add a permanent policy to validate token caps and emit a per-app quota guard.

Samir Patel: follow-ups I'm tracking: - create hard server-side cap of 8192 tokens (not just gateway) - add alert when >5 requests/min with max_tokens > 16384 - add request-level telemetry for token usage in tracing - quick patch to SDK docs to warn about default overrides

Maya Cheng: oncall handoff: I'm handing to @Leo for the postmortem and RCA. I'll be available for follow-up. Severity: Sev2 (customer impact with partial service degraded).

Leo Nguyen: taking handoff. I'll coordinate the postmortem write-up and assign owners for fixes. Immediate priority: ensure quota enforcement is in platform backlog and schedule a hotfix to enforce server caps within 48h.

ops-bot: incident timeline recorded: start=2901234567, mitigated=2901234820, recovered=2901234920, severity=2.

Tara Jenkins: note for follow-up: notify customers that used long-context features, recommend client SDK patch, and offer credits for impacted window.

Maya Cheng: thanks everyone. Adding labels: `oom`, `streaming`, `max_tokens-misconfig`, `customer-impact`. I'll open the postmortem doc and tag owners.

Leo Nguyen: quick action item list: 1) server-side hard token cap (owner: Samir) 2) alert rule for token spikes (owner: Maya) 3) customer comms (owner: Tara) 4) infra: resilient node placement for decode pods (owner: Leo) - target ETA 48h for hotfixes, 2 weeks for infra improvements.

Samir Patel: logging task created: INCIDENT-4312. Uploading logs and snippets to chassis.

Maya Cheng: closing the hands-on page. If anything regresses ping this thread @channel.

ops-bot: thread marked resolved by oncall-bot. Metrics will continue to be monitored for 24h.
